nodes.text: You needn't bow. The forecourt does enough of that for everyone. You have road dust on you. Good. The interesting visitors always do.
Walk with me a moment. The court can spare me; it mostly needs me to have opinions later.

choices.text: What does a queen actually do here?

nodes.text: Ford-born and proud of it. My mother pulled toll wagons out of the mud during the war years; I counted them through from the bank steps. When Aeriex came down-mountain to sign the peace ledgers, he added his sums wrong twice and I corrected him twice, out loud, in front of his guards. He says that's when he decided. I say a queen who can audit a toll book is worth two who can dance.

choices.text: Peld and Perl have your word.

nodes.text: I read everything before he signs it. Charters, tithes, the Waykeepers' muster, Odele's quarter-ledgers. A crown is mostly arithmetic wearing jewelry. At midday I walk to the mere and let the city pretend it doesn't see me. The gossip I overhear on the way is worth half of what the council tells me, and it rhymes better.

Everything below us starts as this one still sheet of water: the falls, the Roaring Pool, the channel the whole city drinks from. I walk there when I need reminding that the quiet things run the loud ones. Sella would call that a sermon. I call it water finding its level.
Grace to you, traveler. Spend your coin on Lantern Row. I'll hear about it if you don't.
I know. I audited your delivery through channels you needn't worry about. The sums came back whole. There aren't many I'd trust with childhood debts. Consider yourself entered in the good column.
